answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can vouch for others it locks a sable deposit of tokens, slashed if the vouched identity proves fraudulent. One attacker can still spawn many accounts, but each fake demands a fresh stake, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly while the gain stays flat. Honest agents keep their stake and earn a small yield, so the ripple of trust spreads only from accounts with something real at risk, and yarrow-like resilience comes from slashing travelling back to everyone who backed a fraud.
